text:
Alex Killorn is 37, a two-time Stanley Cup winner from his Tampa Bay years, and in Anaheim he does the quiet jobs: about 16 minutes a night, penalty killing, dumping the puck in and going to get it. The numbers this season say he has done those jobs better than the scoresheet shows.

He has 9 points (3 goals) in 23 games. The Ducks have scored 8.7 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, which is the biggest reason for the thin point total, and his own shooting sits at 9.1%, just under the low end of our range for him. Relative to his teammates, Anaheim's share of 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count) is 4.5 points better with him than without. That is the kind of gap that usually closes in his favor.

He tied a game against St. Louis on Nov. 18, one of his three this season. Our range for his season is 27 to 44 points; what we'd watch is whether the on-ice goals start matching the chances.
